proposal.title: Campaign timeline — Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy
proposal.reason: Convert this campaign to an independent dated timeline object. Dates are resolved from its execution process without changing precision. Preserve all existing event/subprocess ownership; marketing-step reference_id is absent throughout. Consolidate presentations, campaign material and useful claim-policy requirements into narrated steps; remove historical acceptance labels and duplicate import fragments. Product-owned launch links remain authoritative and validated through the explicit transitional execution mapping. Add the campaign alongside the unchanged execution-process step in process.aurelia_foundation. Legacy duration 44 minutes is preserved as 37 minutes across the nine timed Aurelia blocks plus the separate 7-minute BPI session; untimed sessions and questions are not assigned invented lengths. Both source mentions of BPI leadership are retained; this proposal does not decide a later programme change.

before.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy
before.objective: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.
message: positioning / tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
positioning / academy message: Learn before you decide.
positioning / audience: Nontechnical business owners and managers; secondary audiences are dealers, software developers and peripheral manufacturers.

positioning / partner message: Business Tools organise office work; Abacus supports planning; independent BPI Systems maintains business records. Logix supplies the computer, not ownership of every application.
tagline: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
claim_policy: Legacy acceptance wording (not new confirmation) / status: Accepted alternative-story plan; vendor contracts, measured demonstration performance and unspecified operating details remain execution gates.

acceptance gates / 0: Qualify 500-plus-row workload with stated RAM, populated-cell/formula count, IF and fill-down semantics, measured recalculation and disk loading time; sparse storage is not proof of performance.
acceptance gates / 1: Qualify powered-on attachment at quiescent ports, including electrical sequencing and safe suspension of keyboard polling; no unplugging during printing or disk writes.
acceptance gates / 2: Demonstrate save/close/reopen without loss; printer, disk and projection paths must pass the complete rehearsal.
acceptance gates / 3: Confirm celebrity/partner contracts, venue, Academy cities/course dates, product packages, delivery, warranty and service before publishing definitive claims.
acceptance gates / 4: Measured 48 KB workspace, disk capacity and supported disk configuration; 64 KB or extra drives only when qualified.
acceptance gates / 5: Posting consistency, correction history, disk-full handling and tested backup/restore.
acceptance gates / 6: Readable reports on launch display and supported printers; supported forms and paper documented.
acceptance gates / 7: Payroll jurisdictions, update process and maintenance responsibility explicitly documented.
acceptance gates / 8: Qualify BPI summary export and Abacus import; demonstrate actual sequential applications and label prepared data.

broadcast policy: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions. Offer and supply the material to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix arranges normal duplication and dispatch. Supply station-compatible broadcast copies on request.

Demonstrate qualified AION C IDE editing, optimizing compilation, C/assembly library linkage and calls into the shared ROM TUI. State actual RAM/disk requirements; shared source/API contracts do not imply universal binary compatibility or an already released future target.

Demonstrate syntax highlighting and diagnostic navigation, qualified optimization profiles, an assembly library and a keyboard-operated form with bounded data controls. Show text/bitmap presentation only on tested modes; identify SDK composite helpers separately from native ROM services and publish measured resource/performance results.

stage.label: opening
stage.description: Adam introduces almost four years of development toward an accessible, dependable business assistant; acknowledges the assembled personal computers popularised in 1977.

stage.label: reveal
stage.description: Reveal one Aurelia platform with detachable keyboard and two display choices. Power on colour and 16-shade grayscale systems and show startup; no claim of two different CPU models.

stage.label: editing
stage.description: Prepare a customer quotation letter, demonstrate consistent editing and the copy-buffer; explain how learning transfers between applications.

stage.label: peripherals
stage.description: Attach the self-powered printer at a safely quiescent FlexiBUS port with Aurelia powered on, wait for identification, and print. Once the job finishes, safely interchange printer and keyboard ports and verify both. No removal during traffic or unrestricted hot-plug claim.

stage.label: business_tools
stage.description: Use address book, calendar and calculator in the same customer-order workflow.

stage.label: abacus
stage.description: Safely attach external FDD, load Abacus from diskette, explain a small worksheet, then open a 500-plus-row business document. Raise supplier costs by 8%, show automatic recalculation, add and fill a column using IF to flag low-margin orders, print a short report, save, close and reopen. Use readable worksheet sections on 320x200 launch displays. Use a labelled prepared worksheet with BPI-exported totals; explain their origin. The separate BPI session on 6 June shows the source records and export. Rehearse the shorter slot; retain the full workload for hands-on sessions.

stage.label: partners
stage.description: Gary explains independent CP/M OEM availability, published interfaces and optional extensions; CP/M, hardware and application licenses remain distinct. MPI explains the printer partnership and any separately agreed future FlexiBUS devices. Do not announce the later July SMC agreement. The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with Adam investment and AION/Logix cooperation disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

stage.label: academy
stage.description: Announce Logix Computer Academy in five US cities: learn before you decide, hands-on Fundamentals, configuration advice and direct ordering. Show selected locations, first course dates once finalised. BPI-authorised courses and the dealer programme start July 17; specialist support is provided by BPI.

stage.label: packages
stage.description: State complete package contents, delivery dates, warranty, training and service; invite orders, Academy registration and dealer demonstrations; announce the two technical sessions. Show optional dealer-assembled BPI configurations, separate supplier licences and training and setup arrangements.

stage.label: Aurelia architecture and the open peripheral ecosystem
stage.description: FlexiBUS, display interfaces, implementation/licensing, compatibility and third-party peripheral development.

stage.label: AION C IDE for Aurelia and Developer Package SDK
stage.description: Build and run an application, common TUI behaviour, published interfaces and C source portability without promising universal binary compatibility.

stage.label: premiere / venue
stage.description: Booked auditorium or negotiated NCC presentation slot in Anaheim; access to a main stage is not assumed.

stage.label: premiere / stages / 7 / description
stage.description: Gary explains independent CP/M OEM availability, published interfaces and optional extensions; CP/M, hardware and application licenses remain distinct. MPI explains the printer partnership and any separately agreed future FlexiBUS devices. Do not announce the later July SMC agreement. The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with AION/Logix cooperation and Adam’s accepted investment and AION’s C/TUI redevelopment commitments disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

stage.label: premiere / questions
stage.description: Moderated questions follow the presentation.

stage.label: premiere / display
stage.description: Colour and grayscale launch monitor options; readable 320x200 worksheet sections, not an implied 80-column or whole-document display.

stage.label: technical sessions / 0 / topic
stage.description: Aurelia architecture and the open peripheral ecosystem

stage.label: technical sessions / 1 / topic
stage.description: AION C IDE for Aurelia and Developer Package SDK

stage.label: business sessions / 0 / provider
stage.description: BPI Systems

stage.label: business sessions / 0 / topic
stage.description: Setup, payments, corrections, backups, month-end, inventory and payroll coverage

stage.label: BPI application launch session — 6 June 1978
stage.description: Independent BPI Systems demonstrates a small wholesaler: existing customer/invoice records, incoming payment and remaining balance, receivables/payables and a concise report, then summary export for Abacus. Prepared history is labelled. No live write-back or simultaneous applications. Software presenter explains the workflow; the BPI head speaks in this dedicated session.

marketing_content.description: Proposed 60-second film-trailer-style advertisement; final 10–15 seconds show Aurelia, Abacus, a printed result, logo and June 5 premiere date. Include a recognisable BPI report with its own branding; detailed accounting explanation belongs in print and follow-up films.

Narrator introduces This spring. Douglas discusses a remarkably helpful new assistant during a therapy session. The reveal identifies Aurelia as a computer, and the therapist becomes curious about a demonstration.
Warm humour, concrete business benefits and consistent interaction; avoid unhealthy dependency or claims of speech recognition/artificial intelligence.
Telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demo appointments and Academy bookings; trained staff handle responses.
Small classes, substantial hands-on time, ideally one machine per participant or pair; business tools, introductory Abacus and advice on appropriate configurations and unnecessary purchases.
Order and pay at training centres; immediate collection only where stock is available. No purchase obligation.
Access to a BPI specialist at each launch centre; authorised curriculum and escalation agreement. Training, setup and software licensing are separate.

before.title: Aurelia Foundation and Partnerships
before.description: Establish the commercial and partnership foundation for Aurelia: CP/M implementation, independent BPI cooperation, printer-mechanism supply, ComputerLand distribution and Academy support. Include the Aurelia launch campaign, NCC presentations, the start of BPI training and the dealer programme through the campaign’s end on 17 July 1978. The campaign hierarchy also owns recording, editing and free television distribution of cleared NCC material.

inputs.description: The established DRI partnership enables the Aurelia CP/M implementation agreement that starts this process.
Logix and AION provide the product, engineering and distribution organisation needed to negotiate and carry out the Aurelia partnerships.

outcomes.description: Aurelia has a partnership foundation covering CP/M implementation, OEM printer mechanisms, ComputerLand distribution and Academy support, as documented in the constituent events.

BPI pilot testing, launch qualification and dealer/instructor preparation support the launch of its independently owned Aurelia applications. Qualification gates and support limits remain those recorded in the milestones; BPI has accepted Adam’s investment and AION’s C/TUI redevelopment obligations, with future-platform work and a subsequent BPI share-buyback right.

steps.description: BPI accepts the investment and C/TUI redevelopment agreement.
OEM printer-mechanism agreement.
ComputerLand retail agreement.
BPI business and accountant pilot programme.
Establish and prepare Logix Computer Academy through its dedicated launch-and-training process, from its founding event through 17 July 1978.
BPI and AION engineers tested the application family with businesses and accounting practices, reconciling its reports with existing records.
The partners checked posting, corrections, backup recovery, advertised payroll coverage and the summary export to Abacus.
BPI trained dealers and Academy instructors in the released configurations and its specialist-support arrangements before the June launch.

Run the Aurelia launch and Academy campaign through NCC presentations and the combined BPI training and dealer-programme opening on 17 July 1978. Prepare follow-up plans; completion of this campaign also completes the foundation process.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Use address book, calendar and calculator in the same customer-order workflow.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Safely attach external FDD, load Abacus from diskette, explain a small worksheet, then open a 500-plus-row business document. Raise supplier costs by 8%, show automatic recalculation, add and fill a column using IF to flag low-margin orders, print a short report, save, close and reopen. Use readable worksheet sections on 320x200 launch displays. Use a labelled prepared worksheet with BPI-exported totals; explain their origin. The separate BPI session on 6 June shows the source records and export. Rehearse the shorter slot; retain the full workload for hands-on sessions.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Gary explains independent CP/M OEM availability, published interfaces and optional extensions; CP/M, hardware and application licenses remain distinct. MPI explains the printer partnership and any separately agreed future FlexiBUS devices. Do not announce the later July SMC agreement. The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with {presenter}’s investment, AION/Logix cooperation and AION’s C/TUI redevelopment commitments disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Announce Logix Computer Academy in five US cities: learn before you decide, hands-on Fundamentals, configuration advice and direct ordering. Show selected locations, first course dates once finalised. BPI-authorised courses and the dealer programme start July 17; specialist support is provided by BPI.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. State complete package contents, delivery dates, warranty, training and service; invite orders, Academy registration and dealer demonstrations; announce the two technical sessions. Show optional dealer-assembled BPI configurations, separate supplier licences and training and setup arrangements.
Booked auditorium or negotiated NCC presentation slot in Anaheim; access to a main stage is not assumed.
Moderated questions follow the presentation.
Colour and grayscale launch monitor options; readable 320x200 worksheet sections, not an implied 80-column or whole-document display.

marketing_steps.description: Explain Aurelia architecture and third-party peripheral development.

marketing_presentation.description: FlexiBUS, display interfaces, implementation/licensing, compatibility and third-party peripheral development.

marketing_steps.description: Demonstrate the Aurelia development environment and SDK.

marketing_presentation.description: Build and run an application, common TUI behaviour, published interfaces and C source portability without promising universal binary compatibility.

Demonstrate qualified AION C IDE editing, optimizing compilation, C/assembly library linkage and calls into the shared ROM TUI. State actual RAM/disk requirements; shared source/API contracts do not imply universal binary compatibility or an already released future target.

Demonstrate syntax highlighting and diagnostic navigation, qualified optimization profiles, an assembly library and a keyboard-operated form with bounded data controls. Show text/bitmap presentation only on tested modes; identify SDK composite helpers separately from native ROM services and publish measured resource/performance results.

marketing_steps.description: Present the independent BPI business applications on 6 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Independent BPI Systems demonstrates a small wholesaler: existing customer/invoice records, incoming payment and remaining balance, receivables/payables and a concise report, then summary export for Abacus. Prepared history is labelled. No live write-back or simultaneous applications. Software presenter explains the workflow; the BPI head speaks in this dedicated session.
{provider} covers setup, payments, corrections, backups, month-end, inventory and payroll coverage.

marketing_steps.description: Turn initial interest into informed configuration choices and supported training.

marketing_presentation.description: The Academy was established on {established_date} and is announced publicly on {announcement_date}. Launch in {city_count} US cities with a {fundamentals_days}-day Fundamentals course. Small classes, substantial hands-on time, ideally one machine per participant or pair; business tools, introductory Abacus and advice on appropriate configurations and unnecessary purchases. Order and pay at training centres; immediate collection only where stock is available. No purchase obligation.
BPI-authorised training starts on {start_date}. Access to a BPI specialist at each launch centre; authorised curriculum and escalation agreement. Training, setup and software licensing are separate.

marketing_steps.description: Make the NCC programme available for television coverage.

marketing_presentation.description: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions. Offer and supply the material to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix arranges normal duplication and dispatch. Supply station-compatible broadcast copies on request.

before.title: Aurelia Foundation and Partnerships
before.description: Establish the commercial and partnership foundation for Aurelia: CP/M implementation, independent BPI cooperation, printer-mechanism supply, ComputerLand distribution and Academy support. Include the Aurelia launch campaign, NCC presentations, the start of BPI training and the dealer programme through the campaign’s end on 17 July 1978. The campaign hierarchy also owns recording, editing and free television distribution of cleared NCC material.

inputs.description: The established DRI partnership enables the Aurelia CP/M implementation agreement that starts this process.
Logix and AION provide the product, engineering and distribution organisation needed to negotiate and carry out the Aurelia partnerships.

outcomes.description: Aurelia has a partnership foundation covering CP/M implementation, OEM printer mechanisms, ComputerLand distribution and Academy support, as documented in the constituent events.

BPI pilot testing, launch qualification and dealer/instructor preparation support the launch of its independently owned Aurelia applications. Qualification gates and support limits remain those recorded in the milestones; BPI has accepted Adam’s investment and AION’s C/TUI redevelopment obligations, with future-platform work and a subsequent BPI share-buyback right.

steps.description: BPI accepts the investment and C/TUI redevelopment agreement.
OEM printer-mechanism agreement.
ComputerLand retail agreement.
BPI business and accountant pilot programme.
Establish and prepare Logix Computer Academy through its dedicated launch-and-training process, from its founding event through 17 July 1978.
BPI and AION engineers tested the application family with businesses and accounting practices, reconciling its reports with existing records.
The partners checked posting, corrections, backup recovery, advertised payroll coverage and the summary export to Abacus.
BPI trained dealers and Academy instructors in the released configurations and its specialist-support arrangements before the June launch.

Run the Aurelia launch and Academy campaign through NCC presentations and the combined BPI training and dealer-programme opening on 17 July 1978. Prepare follow-up plans; completion of this campaign also completes the foundation process.
